newsitem.title: FRANCE: French right derailed cars on nuclear waste train.
newsitem.headline: French right derailed cars on nuclear waste train.

text.p: Three derailed wagons from a train carrying spent nuclear fuel have been righted in eastern France near the German and Luxembourg borders and no radiation leaked, French officials said on Wednesday.
"Work went on through the night and the three wagons are now upright and on the rails," Antoinette Janod of the prefect's office for France's Moselle department said by telephone from Metz.

"Verifications are under way concerning the state of the track, the wagons and the cargo. We can't immediately say when the convoy will be able to roll again but we hope to have an idea later today," Janod said.
She said periodic checks showed there was no radiation leak from the cargo of 6.5 tonnes of spent nuclear fuel aboard each of the three wagons.
The mishap occurred early on Tuesday as the convoy, coming from Germany on its way to Britain was derailed at Apach.
The convoy was carrying 18 spent fuel elements from the Lingen power station in Lower Saxony, according to the Lower Saxony environment ministry.
The Metz prefect's office said the convoy belonged to British Nuclear Fuels Plc and was on its way to Dunkirk for shipment to Britain by ferry.
The Saarland state Interior Ministry said the shipment was on its way to the reprocessing plant at Sellafield in northwestern England.

An official in the Apach city hall said the accident had occurred just outside the village of 800 people, on a rail line running alongside the Moselle river. The site is about 500 metres (yards) from the border.
Local residents were not evacuated as officials concluded there was no danger, but emergency workers sealed off the immediate area as a routine precaution.

Germany's opposition Greens party said the accident was one of a series of recent nuclear mishaps including an incident at Britain's Sellafield plant on Sunday in which six workers were contaminated by radioactive dust.
